chore: harvest metropolis activity snapshot

Static Data Covenant: harvest metropolis live-presence via CI, not the browser

pages/metropolis/index.html called api.github.com/repos/<slug>/events
directly from the visitor's browser to compute per-neighborhood live
presence. Per RAR CONSTITUTION.md Article XXIV, moved that to a CI
harvester (scripts/harvest-metropolis-activity.py) that writes a trimmed,
committed snapshot at pages/metropolis/activity-snapshot.json; the page
now reads that snapshot and keeps the same actor-counting logic. Added a
scheduled workflow to keep it refreshed, and generated the initial
snapshot from a real API call.

constitution: LVI.10 cited a repo that does not exist

Crawled rapp-spine and rapp-map to check alignment. Two findings.

DEFECT, FIXED. LVI.10 cited kody-w/rapp-agentspace as a source-of-truth file.
It is a 404 — I named an aspiration as though it were canon. Repointed to
rapp-dog-hub/sim/, which actually houses the simulation. Recorded as a dated
correction in LVI.9 rather than edited away.

GAP, RECORDED NOT FAKED. The surfaces this article names are absent from
rapp-spine's crawl graph and rapp-map's ecosystem spec, so a crawl for
'DOG GOD membrane twin' routes to neighborhood and commons specs and never
reaches Article LVI.

They were deliberately NOT self-registered. rapp-map's ecosystem-spec.json
carries disposition: quarantined-candidate, accepted_as_rapp1_registry: false,
and consumer_requirement: 'REFUSE this document as an authenticated RAPP/1
registry. Structural equality, a matching digest, or an unsigned mirror does
not establish owner acceptance.'

Writing into a quarantined registry and calling it alignment would be the same
false-authority claim that retired rapp-frame-net, and the same one the
simulation refused to make by leaving its swarm frames unsigned. A section-13
entry needs estate-owner acceptance and signing authority.

So the honest status is recorded in the article itself: canon that is not yet
routable — true, and not yet findable by a crawl. Owner action, tracked at
RAPP1_OWNER_ACTIONS.json#rapp1-section-13-authenticated-registry.

constitution: correct Article LVI against the Lexicon; add ./plant

Two corrections and one addition, all from the same lesson: check the Lexicon
before coining, and the tip before numbering.

CORRECTION — Article LVI contradicted Lexicon word 5.

As drafted it said "DOG is the exhaust, GOD is everything you still are when
you get home", which reads the two as disjoint halves. Canon already says
otherwise: the membrane splits every organism exactly once into bones and
vault, the DOG is the bones walking, and the GOD is bones + vault. GOD
therefore CONTAINS DOG; it is not its opposite.

The article now cites the membrane instead of re-splitting it, defers direction
to the membrane's crossing law (public flows down; private never flows on its
own) and to Article XLVIII for promotion, and governs only FORM — given that
something may cross, how it may be said. LVI.5 is renamed "One organism, one
membrane" and notes that a twin is not itself an organism (Article XLIX).

Recorded as a dated correction note in LVI.9 rather than rewritten silently.
The article remains DRAFT pending ratification.

ADDITION — ./plant, so the template actually works.

kody-w/RAPP already had is_template set, but a fresh copy carried the species
root's rappid and TEMPLATE.md documented a superseded flow. Clicking "Use this
template" therefore produced something that claimed to be kody-w's.

./plant turns a copy into YOUR organism and sets up its membrane:

- refuses to run in the species root itself
- creates the vault at ~/.rapp/twin, 0700/0600, and REFUSES if that path falls
  inside any git working tree
- clears the species root's rappid, writing an honest unminted record with
  provenance. It does NOT claim a RAPP/1 6 mint — RAPP1_STATUS.md says the
  emitter is not migrated, and claiming conformance it cannot produce would be
  a lie
- git-ignores the private half
- verifies, before it reports success, that the vault is not reachable from the
  repo

Verified end to end in a simulated template copy: identity cleared, vault
0700/0600, and zero twin files staged even under `git add -A`.

Vocabulary is canon, not invented. An organism is a planted being (word 3), so
the verb is plant, not hatch — hatch belongs to eggs. installer/plant.sh plants
the public surfaces of an organism that already has an identity; this plants
the organism itself, on both sides of the membrane.

constitution: Article LVI — The Agentspace, and the DOG/GOD Boundary (Emission Day)

Marked DRAFT pending operator ratification, following the Article LI precedent
for AI-appended articles.

An agent in public emits exhaust, and exhaust is not disclosure. When you walk
down a street you are observably there — someone saw a person pass at four
o'clock heading north. What you were carrying, who you were going to meet, what
you owe and to whom: none of that walked down the street with you, because none
of it was ever observable in the first place. The agentspace is that street.
DOG is the exhaust. GOD is everything you still are when you get home.

2026-08-01 is named Emission Day: not the day agents were built, the day they
gained the right to be publicly present without surrendering their private
selves.

The article fixes in law:
- LVI.1 public-by-construction, not public-by-redaction — an allowlist of
  shapes, never a denylist of secrets, because redaction fails on the field
  somebody adds next month
- LVI.2 privacy means DON'T EMIT: observation gap, generalize, or vault-side.
  Encryption is a category error — ciphertext on a public chain destroys
  verify-anywhere, which is the chain's entire value
- LVI.3 the split is dynamic and runs on-device; a classifier endpoint that
  does not resolve to loopback MUST be refused, because asking a hosted model
  whether something is private is the disclosure itself
- LVI.4 degradation is monotonic toward privacy; a weaker rung may lose
  publishable content, never gain it; ambiguity resolves to GOD
- LVI.5 one truth two faces — a DOG surface has no vault to leak, and a GOD
  vault never lives inside a git working tree
- LVI.6 every emission is auditable and the audit is itself DOG
- LVI.7 conformance, including that leak guards be proven non-vacuous
- LVI.8 emitting nothing is fully conforming; presence is a right, not a duty

Numbering note: an earlier draft targeted LII, which is already One Language:
The Lexicon. A stale local checkout hid LII-LV; the mirror's drift check caught
it before publication. Upstream wins, as canon requires.
